summary: Backend-only iteration 6 verifying PROMPT 04 payment state-machine & financial invariants. Ran full suite SERIALLY (-n0) as instructed: 75/75 tests pass in 87s (70 pre-existing + 5 new supplemental invariant tests added by this iteration). All acceptance criteria in the review request are verified: (1) centralized validator app/services/payment_state.py — valid transitions allowed (pending->succeeded, pending->failed, succeeded->partially_refunded, partially_refunded->refunded, same-state no-op) and invalid transitions raise InvalidTransition (succeeded->pending, failed->succeeded, cancelled->succeeded, refunded->partially_refunded) [test_payment_state.py::test_valid_transitions_allowed + test_invalid_transitions_rejected 4-param]; (2) no client status injection — POST /api/payments with body {status:'refunded'} still results in server-decided 'succeeded' [test_no_client_status_injection]; (3) idempotent payment creation — two POSTs with same idempotency_key return SAME payment id and NO duplicate ledger credit [test_idempotent_payment_creation + test_success_payment_posts_exactly_one_credit_and_is_idempotent]; (4) idempotent refund — two POSTs with same idem key return SAME refund id and NO duplicate debit; over-refund returns 400 [test_duplicate_and_over_refund + test_refund_posts_single_debit_and_is_idempotent]; (5) full refund makes payment 'refunded' terminal; further refund returns 400 [test_full_refund_then_no_further_refund]; (6) failed sandbox payment (amount_minor % 100 == 13, e.g. 113 & 213) => status 'failed', fee_minor=0, net_minor=0, NO ledger credit posted [test_sandbox_decline_no_ledger_credit + test_failed_payment_posts_no_ledger_credit]; (7) ledger invariants — successful payment posts exactly ONE credit of net_minor with ref_type='payment'; refund posts exactly ONE debit with ref_type='refund'; idempotent replays do NOT add ledger entries (verified by set-diff of ledger IDs before/after) [test_success_payment_posts_exactly_one_credit_and_is_idempotent, test_refund_posts_single_debit_and_is_idempotent]; (8) transition auditability — payment.create and refund.create audit entries carry previous_state, new_state, correlation_id; sensitive-data patterns (bare 16-digit PAN, cvv/cvc, card_number, pan) are NOT present in audit payload [test_audit_contains_state_transition_and_correlation_id, test_refund_audit_has_previous_and_new_state]; (9) authorization preserved — no status-mutation endpoint exists; RBAC + tenant isolation regression coverage in test_authz_isolation.py all still green; (10) regression — payments, refunds, fees, ledger, webhook dispatch, tenant isolation, RBAC all still pass. Code review of payment_engine.py confirms: IntegrityError-catch-and-return-existing pattern on both create_payment and create_refund; validate_transition invoked before setting status; audit changes include previous_state/new_state/correlation_id (correlation_id = payment.id for payment.create and refund.id for refund.create); ledger post_entry called ONLY inside the newly-created branch (never on the idempotent-replay short-circuit). No critical or minor bugs found. No files in app code modified.
critical_code_review_comments: payment_engine.create_payment/create_refund correctly use catch-IntegrityError -> rollback -> re-fetch existing as the concurrency-safe idempotency mechanism, keyed on the (tenant_id, idempotency_key) unique constraint. Ledger post_entry is only invoked in the newly-created branch, so idempotent retries cannot cause duplicate credits/debits. Verified end-to-end.

validate_transition is called BEFORE assigning payment.status in create_payment, and refund success flips payment.status via validate_transition to partially_refunded/refunded. Same-state no-op case is intentionally allowed so idempotent replays don't raise.

Audit entries carry previous_state, new_state, and correlation_id in `changes`. Sensitive-data scan (bare 16-digit PAN starting with 4, cvv/cvc, card_number, pan) found NOTHING in the recorded audit rows. Good.

MINOR (traceability polish, not a bug): /api/ledger/entries currently exposes ref_type + description but NOT ref_id (the model stores ref_id). The tests work around by set-diffing IDs before/after, but exposing ref_id in the response would make external reconciliation easier and directly satisfy 'entries carry ref_type + ref_id traceable to source'. Not blocking.

MINOR (defense-in-depth): the concurrency guarantee relies solely on the DB unique constraint uq_payment_tenant_idem / uq_refund_tenant_idem. That is correct and light-weight, but note that if the provider call is done BEFORE the unique-key insert, a lost race could still cause a real charge for the losing request (the row is discarded but the sandbox side-effect isn't). With the current mock provider this cannot be reproduced, but for real gateways consider inserting a 'pending' payment first (unique-key claim) and only then dispatching to the provider. Documented as a note, not a defect.

PRE-EXISTING (unchanged): pytest.ini defaults to xdist parallel while two webhook tests race on the shared 'acme' tenant -> FK error under -n auto. Serial (-n0) works. Consider scoping webhook tests to a session-unique tenant fixture.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral payments/refunds/audit rows on the seeded 'acme' tenant; no schema or seed changes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Always run backend as: `cd /app/backend && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && python -m pytest tests/ -q -n0`. New test file: /app/backend/tests/test_payment_state_invariants.py verifies ledger single-entry-per-op & audit fields (previous_state/new_state/correlation_id/no-sensitive-data). Ledger API doesn't expose ref_id so tests use set-diff of ledger entry ids by ref_type before/after; if a future prompt adds ref_id to the response, tests will still work.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs. Payment state machine, idempotency (DB unique + IntegrityError catch), single ledger posting per successful op, and audit metadata (previous_state/new_state/correlation_id, sensitive-data-free) are all enforced correctly.
